english: When it dawned, the man went out. He yoked the oxen and [plowed?]. The mother [put] the seed ... and ground it. 'Give us much grain and we will swallow it.' The plow split the field and he sank the seed into it. His wife sang.
uncertain: dʰéǵʰom ... h₁áyso: role unclear (earth acc? bronze gen?)

english: Daughter, stand up quickly; the night is leaving. Go to the ash and look at the fire. If the fire is dying, bring dry branches. Lay them on the hearth and give breath to the flame. Now [it] grew; the flames lick and burn the branches. The fire warms the house and drives away the darkness. Guard the fire through the night. A fireless house grows cold.

The sun's wheel turns, and the work turns with it for us. If the earth thaws/dries, plow. If it is warm, sow. If the grain ripens, cut it with the sickle. If winter comes, sit by the hearth and eat. Now set the plow right and guard the seed. This is the work of a free man.

God-born ..., hear the words of the guardian. Do not throw water on the fire. Do not urinate against the fire and the sun. Fire is a god. The nursing woman(?) has looked at us. Kindle it with dry pine and protect it. The fire watches under the roof at night [and at] dawn.

There was a man who did not love work. When the householder plowed, the lazy man lay under the oak. When he cut with the sickle, the lazy man lay. Winter came. The grain lay in the householder's house. The lazy man was hungry. He came to the householder and asked for something. The householder said: 'Whoever does not plow, he goes hungry.'

If a guest arrives, lead him to the fire. Seat him by the fire and give him a gift. If he has eaten(?), then ask(say?) his name. The guest is dear to the gods. Whoever drives a guest away, the gods strike him. Lay a wool blanket for him and he lies down. If he leaves, give him [gold?/a provision].
